Implement and open a PR for Pattern G of the duplication/over-engineering audit: eliminate duplicated "composition" logic (credential redaction, glob compile-and-filter, diagnostic-line rendering) by putting each on the type that owns the data, plus fold in 2 related dead-code deletions from Pattern A that touch the same files. This is a NEW branch off origin/main (you're in an isolated worktree) — name it `redaction-glob-dedup`.

## 1. Credential redaction (5 copies -> 1 method)

The same one-line body `redact_known_secrets(text, &known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))` is duplicated as a locally-scoped `fn redact_git_stderr`/`redact_stderr` in FIVE places:
- `crates/callisto-conventional/src/pre_cursor.rs` (~18-20)
- `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/pre.rs` (~18-26)
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` (~480-491)
- `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` (~46-54)
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs` (~645-653, named `redact_stderr`)

**Only fix the first FOUR of these.** Leave `publish_client.rs`'s copy alone -- it's being rewritten by separate, parallel work (Pattern C, stacked on top of this branch) that will consume the new helper you're about to add. Don't touch that file at all.

Add the shared method in `crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs` on `CommandOutput`:
```rust
impl CommandOutput {
    /// stderr with known credential values redacted. Prefer over `.stderr`
    /// anywhere the text can reach a user-facing error or log.
    pub fn redacted_stderr(&self) -> String {
        redact_known_secrets(&self.stderr, &known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))
    }
}
```
(Check `redact_known_secrets`/`known_credential_env_values`'s actual signatures in this file first -- match them exactly, don't guess.) Then delete the 4 local `redact_git_stderr` functions and update their call sites to call `.redacted_stderr()` on the relevant `CommandOutput` instead. Also check whether `callisto-moon`'s `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs` (~line 30) and `runner_pdk.rs` (~line 91) construct `CommandOutput`/`CommandError` from raw subprocess stderr with NO redaction at all (per the audit, this crate never had a copy of the redaction fix) -- if so, wire in `.redacted_stderr()` there too as a genuine bug fix (credential leak), not just a refactor.

## 2. Glob compile-and-filter (3 copies -> 1 helper) + fold in 2 dead-code deletions

The pattern `globset::Glob::new(pattern) -> compile_matcher() -> map error` is implemented 3 times:
- `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`: `GitRepository::list_tags` (~257-276), inline
- `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs`: standalone `compile_glob()` (~319-326), used by `ShellGit::list_tags`
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`: `matching_tags()` (~41-56), a third independent copy whose doc comment admits it's "kept in sync" with the vcs crate only by convention

Add one public helper in `callisto-vcs` (e.g. a `TagGlob` newtype or a `pub fn compile_tag_glob(pattern: &str) -> Result<globset::GlobMatcher, VcsError>` -- check `VcsError`'s actual variant name for glob-compile failure, likely `InvalidGlob`, before writing this) built from `shell.rs`'s existing `compile_glob()` logic, made `pub` and reusable. Make `GitRepository::list_tags` call it instead of inlining its own copy. Export it so `callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`'s `matching_tags()` can call it too instead of reimplementing.

**While you're in these exact two files (`crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` and `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`), also delete these two confirmed-dead items** (folded in here specifically because they're the same files, to avoid a separate PR touching them and conflicting):
- `GitVcsProvider` trait in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` (~71-75) plus its sole `impl GitVcsProvider for GitRepository` (~582-590) -- zero other references anywhere in the workspace (verify with a fresh grep first), `GitDataSource` already supersedes it.
- `last_tag_for` (~118-135) and the `select_from_tags` helper it alone calls (~84-91) in `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` -- re-exported from the crate root but the only callers are `last_tag_for`'s own unit tests; `TagIndex::build` uses `select_from_tags_cached` instead. Verify with a fresh grep across the whole workspace (not just this file) before deleting, and remove the `lib.rs` re-export too if it exists.

## 3. Diagnostic-line rendering (1 copy -> reuse existing helper)

`crates/callisto-cli/src/render/mod.rs`: `render_diagnostics` (~11-19) is the established shared helper, called by `render_status`, `render_version`, `render_publish`, `render_publish_report`, `render_matrix`. `render_validate` (~132-142) doesn't call it -- it re-implements the identical `writeln!(w, "  [{:?}] {}", d.severity, d.message)` loop inline. Make `render_validate` call `render_diagnostics` instead.

# Callisto Codebase Guide for Claude & AI Agents

This repository follows the centralized AI agent guidelines documented in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).

---

## Quick Reference

### Primary Task Runner Commands
- `just` / `just ci-fast` (default): Full verification suite minus `coverage`. Use this for everyday pre-PR checks.
- `just ci`: Same, plus `coverage`. Matches CI parity; slow (coverage recompiles the whole workspace under instrumentation).
- `just test` / `moon run :test`: Run all unit, integration, doctests, and E2E lifecycle test suites.
- `just lint` / `moon run :lint`: Run Clippy lints with `-D warnings`.
- `just fmt` / `moon run :format`: Format code automatically.

### Key Architectural Invariants
1. **Safe Rust Only**: `unsafe_code = "forbid"` across all crates.
2. **Format Preservation**: Manifest modifications use CST editors (`toml_edit`, `serde_json` indentation fingerprinting).
3. **Atomic File Persistence**: File edits use `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. **Layer Isolation**: Layer 1 crates (`callisto-model`, `callisto-format`) must remain permissive (`MIT OR Apache-2.0`) and never depend on AGPL crates.
5. **No Emojis in Documentation**: Keep docs clean, technical, scannable, and emoji-free.

### Build/test scoping
Full pipeline: `just ci`/`just test`/`just lint`. For scoped iteration, one direct `cargo test -p <crate>` / `cargo clippy -p <crate>` invocation -- not `moon run <project>:test`, whose per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock (see `Justfile`'s `lint` comment; `moon`'s own `test`/`lint` tasks are literally `cargo test -p $project` / `cargo clippy -p $project` each).

### `Cargo.lock`
Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as pre-commit cleanup -- thrashes the build cache, can turn `just ci` into a multi-hour run. A diff means investigate, not discard.

**Update the managed release PR to use GitHub's forge commit API instead of a local Git push**

`ReleasePrSnapshotV1`, `ReleasePrActionV1`, and `ReleasePrDecisionV1` are replaced by schema-version-2 equivalents: `ReleasePrSnapshotV2`, `ReleasePrActionV2`, and `ReleasePrDecisionV2`. `ReleasePrPullRequestV1`'s `workflow_delta_from_base: bool` is replaced by `ReleasePrPullRequestV2`'s `head_commit: CommitSha`. `ReleasePrActionV2` drops the `Supersede` variant entirely -- there is no replacement, and no runtime fallback to it -- in favor of `Noop`, `Create`, and `Update` variants that name a deterministic staging branch. A new `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1` type builds the typed `createCommitOnBranch` payload from a Git index diff, refusing (with new error codes E149-E154) any `.github/workflows/*` path, non-regular-file Git modes, renames/copies/type-changes, and oversized payloads.

This is consumer-facing: on a public GitHub repository, the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/*` through either the Git push protocol or `createCommitOnBranch`'s own file changes, which previously forced a SHA-suffixed replacement branch and PR (visible churn) whenever a workflow file drifted on the base branch. The new approach never writes that path at all, so the replacement branch behavior is gone and updates land on one stable branch. A branch already replaced under the old behavior remains a valid, ordinary managed branch and keeps being updated in place.
